etymologies.etymologyHTML: Recorded since 1432 as Middle English bogett, bouget, bowgette (“leather pouch”), borrowed from Old French bougette, the diminutive of bouge (“leather bag, wallet”) (also the root of bulge), itself from Late Latin bulga (“leather bag, bellow”), which derives from Gaulish *bolgā (compare Old Irish bolg (“bag”), Breton bolc’h (“flax pod”)), a common root with the Germanic family (compare Dutch balg (“bellows”)), from the Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵʰ-. More at belly.

definitions.definition: (by implication) A relatively small amount of available money.
The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or timeframe.

quote.citation: 1999, Des Lyver, Graham Swainson, Basics of Video Lighting, page 103:
quote.text: At the other extreme, with limitless budgets all they have to do is dream up amazing lighting rigs to be constructed and operated by the huge team of gaffers and sparks, with their generators, discharge lights, flags, gobos and brutes.

quote.citation: 2008, David Mutimer, Canadian Annual Review of Politics and Public Affairs 2002, page 220:
quote.text: The latest Tory budget continued the trend begun in 2000 by making further small cuts in family income taxes.

quote.citation: 2009, Andrew Paquette, Computer Graphics for Artists II: Environments and Characters:
quote.text: The most common poly budget in use for games at the time of this writing is between 5,000 and 10,000 tris.

definitions.definition: An itemized summary of intended expenditure; usually coupled with expected revenue.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto X”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: With that out of his bouget forth he drew / Great store of treasure, therewith him to tempt  […]

quote.citation: 2020, Hilary Mantel, The Mirror and the Light, Fourth Estate, page 364:
quote.text: The king holds up a hand to the lute player: ‘Thank you, leave us.’ The boy stuffs his music back into his budget and goes out backwards.

quote.citation: 1912, Arthur Conan Doyle, The Lost World […], London; New York, N.Y.: Hodder and Stoughton, →OCLC:
quote.text: I set off, therefore, in high spirits, for I felt that I had done good work and was bringing back a fine budget of news for my companions.

definitions.definition: (obsolete, military) A socket in which the end of a cavalry carbine rests.

quote.citation: 1991 December, “The YS Official Top 100 Part 3”, in Your Sinclair, number 72:
quote.text: A classic budget game, there isn't really anything outstanding about Rescue at all.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To construct or draw up a budget.
(transitive) To provide funds, allow for in a budget.
(transitive) To plan for the use of in a budget.
